title: Two-phase commit: both databases vote yes, the coordinator dies, and the rows stay locked
captions: Order 42 must change two databases. The coordinator sends PREPARE to both. Each one writes the changes to disk, but does not commit yet.
Both databases vote YES. A YES is a promise: I can commit, even after a crash. To keep that promise, each one keeps its row locks.
The coordinator writes COMMIT to its own log. That is the decision. Then its machine dies before it tells anyone.
Both databases are now in doubt. They voted YES, so they may not abort alone. They do not know the decision, so they may not commit. Locked rows block other orders.
Classic 2PC waits for the coordinator to come back. Spanner and CockroachDB store the decision in a Paxos or Raft group instead, so it survives one machine dying and the commit can still finish.
